idea.title: Cross-Lingual Transferability of Abstention Thresholds in Factual Question Answering: A Case Study on Urdu
idea.research_problem: Investigating whether abstention thresholds calibrated on English factual question answering models remain reliable when deployed on translated Urdu questions, and whether a small separate Urdu calibration set can mitigate cross-lingual reliability gaps in coverage and accuracy.
idea.research_gap: Bounded search findings indicate that while calibration and multi-granularity evaluation have been studied extensively for high-resource languages, the cross-lingual transfer of uncertainty-based abstention mechanisms to low-resource languages like Urdu remains unexplored, particularly under translation artifacts and morphological differences.
idea.methodology: We employ an open-source language model accessed via API or running locally under hardware constraints. We evaluate zero-shot factual question answering on an English dataset and its translated Urdu counterpart. We measure model confidence using verbalized probabilities and entropy over generated tokens. We establish an English-calibrated abstention threshold to maximize a target precision-recall trade-off. We then evaluate its zero-shot transfer performance on Urdu. Finally, we implement a small-scale post-hoc threshold adjustment using a minimal, held-out Urdu validation set to re-calibrate the abstention cutoff.
idea.expected_contribution: We expect to demonstrate that direct transfer of English-calibrated abstention thresholds leads to degraded selective prediction performance in Urdu due to calibration shift. We hypothesize that a minimal, language-specific calibration subset restores selective accuracy and balances the coverage-accuracy frontier.
idea.experimental_setup: We use a subset of English open-domain QA datasets and translate them into Urdu using a standard public translation pipeline. We evaluate open-weights LLMs that support Urdu. We compare uncalibrated English thresholds against re-calibrated thresholds using a 200-sample Urdu development set, measuring selective accuracy and risk-coverage curves.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate performance using area under the risk-coverage curve (AURCC), selective accuracy at fixed coverage levels (e.g., 80% coverage), and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on both English and Urdu evaluation splits.
feasibility_assumptions: Publicly available translation pipelines provide sufficiently fluent Urdu questions for semantic evaluation.
A 12GB consumer GPU or standard API access is adequate for running inference and computing token-level uncertainty metrics over evaluation splits.
A small development set of 200 translated instances is sufficient for robust threshold re-calibration.

assumption_checks.assumption: English-calibrated uncertainty thresholds transfer directly to Urdu without severe over-abstention.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Apply the English-derived threshold to the translated Urdu zero-shot set and measure absolute coverage drop.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: Coverage does not deviate by more than 15% from the target operational level.
assumption_checks.fallback: If coverage drops precipitously, abandon direct transfer and mandate immediate quantile-based threshold resetting on the small Urdu validation split.

assumption_checks.assumption: A 200-sample Urdu calibration set provides stable threshold estimation without overfitting.
assumption_checks.validation_step: Perform 5-fold cross-validation on the Urdu development split to measure variance in the optimal threshold.
assumption_checks.acceptance_criterion: Standard deviation of the selected threshold across folds remains below 5% of the total uncertainty range.
assumption_checks.fallback: If variance is high, pool uncertainty estimates using nearest-neighbor similarity features from the English training distribution.

prior_work_comparison.shared_mechanism: Utilizes uncertainty metrics derived from language model generations to guide prediction and filtering.
prior_work_comparison.proposed_difference: Focuses on cross-lingual transfer and post-hoc threshold adjustment for low-resource languages rather than reinforcement learning-based retrieval ranking in English.
prior_work_comparison.verification_needed: Verify whether uncertainty score distributions maintain rank-order correlation across languages.

prior_work_comparison.shared_mechanism: Evaluates model knowledge limits and uncertainty alignment in open-domain question answering.
prior_work_comparison.proposed_difference: Addresses cross-lingual calibration shifts in abstention decisions rather than multi-granularity response aggregation.
prior_work_comparison.verification_needed: Confirm that multi-granularity correctness scoring does not interact adversely with cross-lingual token uncertainty.

idea.core_hypothesis: Uncertainty-based abstention thresholds calibrated on English factual QA exhibit systematic miscalibration when transferred to Urdu due to translation artifacts and language-specific entropy shifts, which can be corrected using a minimal target-language calibration set.
idea.distinctive_mechanism: A targeted post-hoc threshold re-calibration technique operating on a small, low-resource validation set to align the risk-coverage frontier across linguistic boundaries.
idea.minimum_test: Evaluate an open-source LLM on 500 English QA pairs and their Urdu translations, comparing the selective accuracy of an English-optimized abstention threshold against a re-calibrated threshold using a 200-sample Urdu dev set.

idea.title: Cross-Lingual Transferability of Abstention Thresholds in Factual Question Answering: A Case Study on Urdu
idea.research_problem: Investigating whether abstention thresholds calibrated on English factual question answering models remain reliable when deployed on translated and native Urdu questions, and whether a small separate Urdu calibration set can mitigate cross-lingual reliability gaps in coverage and accuracy.
idea.research_gap: Bounded search findings indicate that while calibration and multi-granularity evaluation have been studied extensively for high-resource languages, the cross-lingual transfer of uncertainty-based abstention mechanisms to low-resource languages like Urdu remains underexplored, particularly under translation artifacts, morphological differences, and tokenization gaps.
idea.methodology: We employ an open-source language model accessed locally under hardware constraints. We evaluate zero-shot factual question answering on an English dataset alongside its translated Urdu counterpart and a supplementary human-curated native Urdu subset to isolate translation noise. We measure model confidence using sequence-aggregated token entropy and verbalized probabilities. We establish an English-calibrated abstention threshold to maximize a target precision-recall trade-off. We then evaluate its zero-shot transfer performance on Urdu and implement a post-hoc quantile-based threshold adjustment using a minimal, held-out Urdu validation set.
idea.expected_contribution: We expect to demonstrate that direct transfer of English-calibrated abstention thresholds leads to degraded selective prediction performance in Urdu due to calibration shift and translation artifacts. We hypothesize that a minimal, language-specific calibration subset restores selective accuracy and balances the coverage-accuracy frontier.
idea.experimental_setup: We use a subset of English open-domain QA datasets translated into Urdu using a standard public pipeline, alongside a small native Urdu validation subset. We evaluate open-weights LLMs that support Urdu. We compare uncalibrated English thresholds against re-calibrated thresholds using a 200-sample Urdu development set, measuring selective accuracy and risk-coverage curves.
idea.evaluation_strategy: We evaluate performance using area under the risk-coverage curve (AURCC), selective accuracy at fixed coverage levels (e.g., 80% coverage), and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on both English and Urdu evaluation splits, incorporating bootstrapping to report confidence intervals.
feasibility_assumptions: Publicly available translation pipelines provide sufficiently fluent Urdu questions for semantic evaluation when combined with native test subsets.
A 12GB consumer GPU is adequate for running inference and computing token-level uncertainty metrics over evaluation splits without full model training.
A small development set of 200 translated instances is sufficient for robust threshold re-calibration when coupled with stability checks.
